blocks.text: Present day living is the enemy of the human body. When our ancestors came down from the trees a million or two years ago, they lived an active hunting life, running to catch their food, fighting off predators, struggling to keep warm at night. Modern cities make no such demands on us. Many of us ride to work in our cars or on public transport, work all day at a desk, then slouch in front of the television at night. It’s not surprising that our bodies become flabby, stiff and fat.

So the main reason for improving your physical fitness is simply to get more Joy out of life. Your body was meant to be used, and when you have given it back its strength and vitality, you will develop a happier, more confident out-look on life as a whole.

The other reason for physical exercise is more sobering. Just as when you leave your car in the garage and don’t take it out for a regular spin, the tires go flat, the body work rusts and the battery runs down, so the body that is not exercised begins to degenerate. Unfit, overweight people have a greater than average chance of arthritis, breathing trouble, low back pain and accidents. And there is a lot of evidence that people who do not exercise have a greater chance of developing one of the big killers of our time – heart disease and high blood pressure. Unfit people only live half a life and all too often it ends abruptly…

blocks.text: Robert Brown and his girlfriend Ann play tennis twice a week.

items: *Ann:* Hello?
*Robert:* Hello, is Ann there?
*Ann:* This is Ann.
*Robert:* Hi, Ann. This is Robert.
*Ann:* Oh, Robert. Nice to hear your voice.
*Robert:* Well, I just called to see if you’d like to play tennis this afternoon.
*Ann:* Oh, sure. I’d love to. I’ll see you at the club at 5 o’clock this afternoon.
*Robert:* By the way, did you go to the club yesterday?
*Ann:* Yes, I did. And I played against Laura Adams. You know, that nice blonde we met at Lou’s party. She’s really good.
*Robert:* So she beat you.
*Ann:* No, incredible as it may sound, she didn’t win…I did!
*Robert:* No kidding?
*Ann:* No kidding at all. But things were really hard. She was ahead by three games and … suddenly the lights went out! We had to wait for about half an hour to complete the first set.
*Robert:* And then what happened?
*Ann:* She finally took the first set 6-2.
*Robert:* That wasn’t a good start for you.

*Ann:* It really wasn’t. But her happiness didn’t last very long. I rushed her and didn’t let her think. Her shots started going wild, she got nervous and you see the result, I won the other two sets.
*Robert:* She didn’t seem to be playing just for the fun of it.
*Ann:* That’s right. She took it very seriously.
*Robert:* How about you? I bet you like to win too.
*Ann:* Yes, but I’m not the competitive type. I wouldn’t get angry if I lost a set or a tournament.
*Robert:* Well… good for you. See you later.
*Ann:* O.K.
